service.name: Modern jazz trio
service.serviceType: Modern jazz guitar trio for cocktail hours, dinners, galas and private events
service.description: A Denver jazz guitar trio, Doug Emery, Sri Viswanath and Brian Jaffe, playing the standards with a modern edge as a trio or as a quartet with saxophone, for cocktail hours, dinners, galas, weddings and private events across Denver, the Front Range and the Colorado mountain corridor.

faqs.q: What does Changes Jazz Trio play?
faqs.a: Jazz standards, played by a guitar trio with a modern edge: guitar, fretless bass and drums, with the arrangements left open. It's instrumental, so it sits under a dinner without competing with the conversation, and it holds a listening crowd when the evening gives it one. Their site carries two studio recordings.

faqs.q: How is this different from the jazz duo?
faqs.a: The jazz duo is a format we guarantee by instrumentation: upright bass and guitar playing standards for cocktails and dinner. Changes is a named working trio with drums and a fretless bass, a more modern sound, and three players you can look up. Book the duo for the hour, and Changes when you want a band with a name on it.

Yes. The quartet is the trio plus saxophone, which puts a horn on the melody and turns a dinner set into a featured one. It's the size for a gala or a client dinner where the music is part of the program.

The trio plays cocktails and dinner at 65 to 72 dBA at the nearest table, a level the table talks across. A featured set runs louder on purpose, and if your venue has a decibel cap, give us the number and the set is built under it.
Denver. All three players live and work in the Denver metro, and the trio plays the Front Range and the mountain towns on the same terms as the rest of the roster.

Yes, with a covered, level and dry performance area and power run to it. We agree a move-indoors plan with you ahead of time, because Colorado evenings turn fast and the electronics stop behaving in the wet.
